name: Bharwa Karela
subtitle: bitter gourds stuffed with sharp onion masala and cooked down slow until the skins wrinkle

ingredients.note: half for the stuffing, half for the salting

ingredients.qty: 2 tsp for salting, plus to taste

prepNotes: Scrape, slit and salt the karela at least 1 hour before cooking, and 3 hours is better. This is the only step that actually removes bitterness.
Keep the scraped peel. Fried into the stuffing it adds a good rough texture. Discard it if you want the mildest version.
Have kitchen string or toothpicks ready to tie the stuffed gourds shut.

steps.text: Scrape the ridged skin off each karela with a knife, reserving the scrapings. Slit each one lengthways down one side without cutting through, and scoop out the seeds.
Rub the gourds inside and out with 2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp turmeric and leave in a colander for 1-3 hours. Squeeze out the brown liquid and rinse once.
steps.tip: Squeeze hard. That bitter brown water is exactly what you are trying to get rid of.

steps.text: Heat 3 tbsp mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, cool for 30 seconds, then crackle the mustard seeds and crushed fenugreek.
Add the onion and the reserved scrapings and fry 10-12 minutes on medium until golden and dry.
Stir in the fennel, coriander, cumin, remaining turmeric, chilli powder, amchur, garam masala, green chilli and salt. Fry 3 minutes until the mixture smells toasted and looks dry.
steps.tip: The stuffing must be dry. Wet stuffing leaks out and steams the gourds instead of frying them.

steps.text: Cool the masala, fold in the coriander leaves, then pack it firmly into each karela and tie shut with string.
Heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil in a wide pan and lay the gourds in a single layer.
Cook uncovered on low for 25-30 minutes, turning every 5 minutes, until the skins are wrinkled, blistered and dark in patches.
steps.tip: Low and slow, uncovered. Covering the pan makes them soggy and grey.

steps.text: Press one with a spoon. It should give completely. Rest 5 minutes, snip the strings and serve with dal and roti.

storage: Keeps 4 days refrigerated and tastes better on day two. Reheat dry in a pan on low for 5 minutes; do not microwave, which makes the skins rubbery.
